chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Faddal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from his father, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that

Suleyman ibn Dawood (peace be upon him) performed Hajj of the House (Kaaba) accompanied by the Jinn and the humans, and the birds, and the winds, and he clothed the House with Egyptian linen (qabati cloth).

key_terms.الرِّيَاحِ: The winds — Suleyman (AS) was granted control over the wind, enabling miraculous travel
key_terms.الْبَيْتَ: The House — refers to the Kaaba in Mecca, the central sanctuary of Islam, believed to have been built by the Prophets Ibrahim and Isma'il (AS)
key_terms.الْجِنِّ: Jinn — invisible beings created from fire, who along with humans are accountable to God and capable of faith or disbelief; Suleyman (AS) had authority over them
key_terms.الْقَبَاطِيَّ: Qabati — fine white Egyptian linen (from 'Qibt', the Arabic name for the Coptic Egyptians), historically the most prized textile for draping the Kaaba

ai.seo_question: Did Prophet Suleyman (Solomon) perform Hajj to the Kaaba according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration, transmitted by Imam al-Baqir (AS) through the companion Zurara, reports that the Prophet Suleyman (Solomon, peace be upon him) performed the pilgrimage to the Kaaba leading an extraordinary retinue of jinn, humans, birds, and the winds — all subject to his divinely granted dominion. He also adorned the House of God with fine Egyptian linen (al-qabati), a prized cloth from Egypt. This account situates the Hajj as an ancient, universally observed act of worship practiced by the greatest of prophets, emphasizing continuity between the Abrahamic prophetic tradition and Islam.
